Notes: The b* block of the deposit, identified by the authors' ATP/HH/AE/RT subscale columns and by matching MPATS's published 16-item length. `b8` appears twice in the header; positionally the second is b9 and is restored as such.

Description: Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), 36 items on a 1-5 scale, Israeli community sample. 8,385 responses from 233 respondents on 36 items.

Description: Malay Internet Addiction Test (M-IAT), 20 items on a 0-5 scale, Malaysian adolescents. 8,400 responses from 420 respondents on 20 items.
Reference: Md Bukhori AB, Ja'afar MH (2024). Internet addiction among adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic: Associations with sociodemographic and psychological distress. PeerJ, 12, e17489. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.17489
Notes: The deposited SurveyMonkey export has a TWO-ROW header (block label above item wording); read as a single header row the items collapse into `Unnamed:` columns, which is why upstream triage saw no item structure. Items are numbered from the source's own numbering within each block. Total Score columns are composites and are excluded.

Description: Malay DASS-21, 21 items on a 0-3 scale, Malaysian adolescents. 8,820 responses from 420 respondents on 21 items.
Reference: Md Bukhori AB, Ja'afar MH (2024). Internet addiction among adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic: Associations with sociodemographic and psychological distress. PeerJ, 12, e17489. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.17489
Notes: From the same two-row-header export as bukhori_2024_iat; see that table's note.

Description: Political knowledge battery, 6 binary items, US survey respondents. 16,815 responses from 2,807 respondents on 6 items.
Reference: Fitz EB, Stecuła DA, Hitt MP, Saunders KL (2024). Objective numeracy exacerbates framing effects from decision-making under political risk. Scientific reports, 14, 10473. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-61099-y
Notes: The article is CC BY; the data are deposited separately at Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/MMOGJI) and were reached from the paper's Data Availability statement. These 6 items are already scored 0/1 in the deposit.

Description: Objective numeracy battery, 11 binary-scored items, US survey respondents; resp_raw carries the original free-text answer. 30,722 responses from 2,806 respondents on 11 items.
Reference: Fitz EB, Stecuła DA, Hitt MP, Saunders KL (2024). Objective numeracy exacerbates framing effects from decision-making under political risk. Scientific reports, 14, 10473. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-61099-y
Notes: Nine of the eleven items are free text in the deposit ('50%', 'half the time', 'about 500'). Scoring is not a judgment made here: the authors' replication .do file enumerates every string they counted as correct, and the processing script parses that file at run time and applies it. numeracy4 and numeracy5 are multiple choice and the .do recodes them by option number (3 and 2 correct). One deliberate difference from the authors' Stata: their recode scores a BLANK as incorrect; a blank is a non-response, so blanks are dropped here instead (14-33 per item out of 2,813). Data DOI 10.7910/DVN/MMOGJI.

Description: Joint Simon task, capuchin monkeys, trial-level accuracy. Items are the stimulus probe (experimental condition crossed with trial type, 16 in all); compatibility travels as an item covariate because trial type determines it exactly. resp is the experiment program's own correctness scoring. 2,753 responses from 10 subjects on 16 items.
Reference: Martínez M, Babb MH, Range F, Brosnan SF (2024). The Joint Simon task is not joint for capuchin monkeys. Scientific Reports, 14, 5937. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-55885-x
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). Trials where the monkey did not respond carry a third code (2) in the source's scoring column and are dropped rather than scored 0 -- 49 here. The deposit's correct_rv string column labels those inconsistently (9 of 49 as 'correct') and is not used. Monkey names are lowercased because the two sheets disagree on case.

Description: Go/no-go control task from the same capuchin study, trial-level accuracy, 8 stimulus probes (reward/no-reward crossed with trial type). 712 responses from 10 subjects on 8 items.
Reference: Martínez M, Babb MH, Range F, Brosnan SF (2024). The Joint Simon task is not joint for capuchin monkeys. Scientific Reports, 14, 5937. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-55885-x
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). 88 no-response trials dropped; see martinez_2024_joint_simon for the scoring note.

Description: Detour task measuring inhibitory control in 8 bearded dragons and 24 tortoises. Items are the 20 trials in order (4 days x 5 trials), complete for every animal; read them as a learning sequence rather than as distinct probes. resp is 1 when the animal detoured successfully. 640 responses from 32 subjects on 20 items.
Reference: Santacà M, Wilkinson A, Stancher G, Sovrano VA, Bisazza A (2025). Lizards and tortoises show evidence of low inhibitory control. Scientific Reports, 15, 23446. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-08373-9
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). id is the species prefixed onto the source Subject, because the dragons are named and the tortoises numbered. The deposit's Time_log is not emitted as rt: the standard requires seconds and the log's base is unstated (log10 gives 3-256s, natural log 1.6-11.1s, both plausible).

Description: Spontaneous-alternation T-maze, 21 adult rats, five sessions of 20 trials. resp is WHICH ARM the rat entered (1 = right, 0 = left), NOT whether it was correct: no arm is correct in this task and the construct the authors measure, alternation, is a property of consecutive trials. Do not model resp as accuracy. 1,077 responses from 21 subjects on 100 items.
Reference: Acevedo-Triana CA, Rojas MJ, Cardenas FP (2017). Running wheel training does not change neurogenesis levels or alter working memory tasks in adult rats. PeerJ, 5, e2976. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.2976
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). The sheet's summary rows (Animals == 'TOTAL') are dropped, as are the Hab* habituation phases, which have no trials. Only 1,077 of 2,100 trials have an arm entry recorded; the other 1,022 have Right and Left both 0 (no entry within the time limit) and are dropped as non-responses, plus one row with both set to 1, which cannot be a single choice. The deposit's Alternation column is a per-session total on the summary rows, not a trial-level response, and is not used.

Description: AI models as respondents: 124 large language models (id = model name, verbatim, aliases not merged) scored on the 541 prompts of IFEval, an instruction-following benchmark whose prompts each carry 1-3 programmatically verifiable instructions (e.g. no commas, at least 300 words). resp is the number of the prompt's instructions the model's response satisfied under IFEval's strict check (0 to itemcov_n_instructions); resp == itemcov_n_instructions is prompt-level strict accuracy. From the OpenEval archive (Hugging Face Open-Eval-Commons/OpenEval, revision 23a1ded9), one run, scores only. Respondents are not independent: many models share base weights, decoding temperature varies across models (cov_temperature), and items may appear in training data.
Reference: Jiang, H., Zhang, S., Zhu, D., Bai, Y., Truong, S. T., Yi, X., Koyejo, S., Xie, X., & Xiao, Z. (2026). AI Evaluation Should Require Standardized Item-Level Data Releases. arXiv:2604.03244 (v2). Benchmark: Zhou, J., et al. (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911.
Notes: CC BY-NC 4.0 is authoritative per the OpenEval authors (email to Ben Domingue, 2026-09-16), who granted inclusion of the model x item score tables with credit to the repository and paper; the HF card says the same, the GitHub repo carries no licence. NC inclusion approved by Ben 2026-09-19 (irw#2166). Scores only: no item text or model output, since the grant does not cover benchmark content. Permission on file at licenseinfo/emails/openeval_jiang_2026.md.

Reference: López-Odar, D., Aguirre-Morales, M., Cirilo-Acero, I., Hervias-Guerra, E., Vara-Horna, A., & Deza-Villanueva, S. (2025). Notes: The ERQ block in the same deposit is NOT in IRW: the paper documents the Peruvian ERQ as 7-point (1-7) and the deposited ERQ1-ERQ10 hold five levels 0-4 across all 403 respondents, so the responses cannot be mapped to the documented anchors. Held pending an author query. Item text not shipped -- BERQ is a third-party instrument (Kraaij & Garnefski 2019; Spanish adaptation Dominguez-Lara et al. 2022) and the deposit is a plain CSV with positional column names and no labels of any kind.

Description: General Health Questionnaire GHQ-28 (Goldberg & Hillier 1979), 28 items in four seven-item dimensions (somatic symptoms, anxiety, social dysfunction, depression), administered to the same 403 Peruvian adults as lopezodar_2025_berq. 11,284 responses on the documented 4-point scale, 0 (not at all) to 3 (much more than usual).
Reference: López-Odar, D., Aguirre-Morales, M., Cirilo-Acero, I., Hervias-Guerra, E., Vara-Horna, A., & Deza-Villanueva, S. (2025). Description: ICF-RS-17, a 17-item functional assessment tool built from the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health via a three-round Delphi study, then validated on 2,574 inpatients at 12 Chinese rehabilitation institutions (Nanjing, Wuxi, Suzhou, Aug 2021-Mar 2023). Each patient was rated on all 17 ICF categories at admission and again at discharge, so wave 1 = admission and wave 2 = discharge; 87,516 responses. resp is the 0-10 Numerical Rating Scale the paper defines, where 0 = no problem and 10 = complete problem -- HIGHER IS WORSE functioning. item is the ICF category code as the source spells it (d450, b455, ...).
Reference: Li, J., Xu, G., Jin, J., Li, N., Li, J., & Liu, S. (2025). Development and validation of a functional assessment tool for Chinese inpatient rehabilitation: insights from a Delphi study based on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF). PeerJ, 13, e20280. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.20280
Notes: 35 rows (16 profiles) in the source file are exact duplicates across all 37 columns; two patients matching on all 34 ratings of an 0-10 scale is not a coincidence and the profiles are not degenerate. They are KEPT rather than dropped: the file has no id column, the paper's own N is 2,574, and removing them would publish a different sample than the article analyses. Users who need de-duplicated data can drop ids whose full response profile is identical. The b/d item prefixes are ICF's own chapter codes (body functions / activities and participation), not two instruments -- the paper validates ICF-RS-17 as a single two-factor tool, so do not split it. Item text not yet shipped: the 17 ICF category names are in the paper's Tables 3-4 (paper_explicit, needs a Step 5b verification), not in the data file.

Description: Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS; Hendrick 1988), Polish translation by Monfort et al. Reference: Adamczyk, K., Kleka, P., & Frydrychowicz, M. (2022). Psychometric functioning, measurement invariance, and external associations of the Relationship Assessment Scale in a sample of Polish adults. Scientific Reports, 12, 22077. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-26653-6
Notes: IMPORTANT -- items 4 and 7 are harmonised. The three samples do not agree on how the two negatively worded items are stored: validation sample 1 deposits them raw (RAS4 mean 1.88) alongside explicit reverse-scored copies (RAS4_R mean 4.12, r = -1.0), while the reference sample and validation sample 2 deposit only the reverse-scored direction (means 4.24 and 4.15). This table uses the reverse-scored column for validation sample 1, so all three samples run the same direction for every item -- after harmonisation RAS4 reads 4.24/4.12/4.15 and RAS7 reads 3.65/3.59/3.49 across the samples. Nothing was recomputed: the reversed columns are the depositors' own. Consequence for item text: for items 4 and 7 the shipped resp runs OPPOSITE to the A-E anchors printed in the deposit's materials document. From the OSF deposit's SPSS files. No variable labels and no value labels on any item column in any of the three files -- both levels checked -- so item text has no data_labels route; the deposit's materials document prints the Polish wording for several of these instruments and is the source a later itemtext pass should use.

Reference: Zorowitz, S., Chierchia, G., Blakemore, S.-J., & Daw, N. D. (2024). An item response theory analysis of the matrix reasoning item bank (MaRs-IB). Behavior Research Methods, 56(3), 1104-1122.

Reference: Jiang, H., Zhang, S., Zhu, D., Bai, Y., Truong, S. T., Yi, X., Koyejo, S., Xie, X., & Xiao, Z. (2026). AI Evaluation Should Require Standardized Item-Level Data Releases. arXiv:2604.03244 (v2). Benchmark: Lin, B. Y., et al. (2025). WildBench: Benchmarking LLMs with Challenging Tasks from Real Users in the Wild. ICLR 2025. https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/poster/29940
Notes: CC BY-NC 4.0 is authoritative per the OpenEval authors (email to Ben Domingue, 2026-09-16), who granted inclusion of the model x item score tables with credit to the repository and paper and stated that all response data then in OpenEval were managed by them; read at the revision in place that day (hi_tom/emobench at a later revision that only removes duplicates). NC inclusion approved by Ben (irw#2166; widened beyond ifeval 2026-09-30). Scores only: no item text, model output or judge rationale, since the grant does not cover benchmark content. Permission on file at licenseinfo/emails/openeval_jiang_2026.md.

Description: NFL field goal and extra point attempts, 1999-2025 seasons (regular season and playoffs), one row per kick: 61,267 kicks by NFL kickers. id = kicker (GSIS id); item = kind of kick (extra_point, or field goal distance band fg_18_29, fg_30_39, fg_40_49, fg_50_plus); resp = 1 if made/good, 0 if missed, failed or blocked. Coaches decide when to attempt a field goal and send stronger kickers out for longer ones, so make rates mix kicker skill with kick selection; exact distance in trial_dist. trial_ columns also carry blocked flag, season, playoff, game id, game clock, home/away, score margin, roof, surface, temperature and wind. Real-data counterpart to the simulated nbashots_sim.
Reference: nflverse (2026). nflverse-data: play-by-play data, release pbp [Data set]. https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data
Notes: Licence from the nflverse-data LICENSE file (CC BY 4.0), checked 2026-09-30. The play-by-play derives from the NFL GSIS feed. Built by data/trials/nflverse_kicks.R; 31 aborted extra points (no kick) dropped. The extra point moved from about 20 to 33 yards in 2015. irw#2626.

Description: NFL pass attempts, 2006-2025 seasons (regular season and playoffs), one row per throw: 366,274 throws by 616 passers. id = passer (GSIS id); item = target zone, depth by air yards (behind the line, short 0-9, medium 10-19, deep 20+) crossed with direction (left, middle, right); resp = 1 if completed. Quarterbacks choose where to throw, so completion rates mix passing skill with target selection; exact air yards in trial_airyards. trial_ columns also carry interception flag, targeted receiver id, down, distance to go, field position, shotgun, no-huddle, QB hit, season, playoff, game id, game clock, home/away, score margin and roof. Sacks, spikes and two-point tries excluded; throwaways count as incompletions. Real-data counterpart to the simulated nbashots_sim.
Reference: nflverse (2026). nflverse-data: play-by-play data, release pbp [Data set]. https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data
Notes: Licence from the nflverse-data LICENSE file (CC BY 4.0), checked 2026-09-30. The play-by-play derives from the NFL GSIS feed. Built by data/trials/nflverse_passes.R; starts 2006, the first season with air yards. 1,990 throws missing air yards or location dropped; 59 throws (mostly 2006-2010) have implausible air yards below -20 and are kept as recorded. irw#2626.

Description: Soccer shots from Wyscout match event logs, one row per shot: 45,942 shots by 2,386 players in every match of the 2017-18 English, French, German, Italian and Spanish first divisions, the 2018 World Cup and Euro 2016 (1,941 matches). id = player (Wyscout id); item = kind of shot (foot, head, free_kick, penalty); resp = 1 if a goal. Players choose when and where to shoot, so conversion rates mix finishing skill with shot selection; shot location in trial_locx/trial_locy (percent of pitch) with distance (m) and goal-mouth angle derived. trial_ columns also carry competition, match id, game clock, shoot-out flag, home/away (league matches only) and counter-attack flag. Real-data counterpart to the simulated nbashots_sim.
Reference: Pappalardo, L., Cintia, P., Rossi, A., Massucco, E., Ferragina, P., Pedreschi, D., & Giannotti, F. (2019). A public data set of spatio-temporal match events in soccer competitions. Scientific Data, 6, 236.

Description: MECO L1 reading comprehension: 12 short expository texts read in the reader's first language during eye-tracking, each followed by 4 yes/no questions (48 items; resp = 1 correct, 0 incorrect). Only 5 texts are translations of a common original; item codes are shared only for those questions (text{t}_q{q}), and every other item is specific to a language or text version, so the table is sparse by design. Reference: Repetto, C., Rodella, C., Conca, F., Santi, G. C., & Catricalà, E. (2022). The Italian Sensorimotor Norms: Perception and action strength measures for 959 words. Behavior Research Methods, 55(8), 4035-4047.
Notes: Built from the ratings_ sheet of DATA/data all participants_.xlsx (OSF rcsnm, CC BY-NC 4.0 on the node). Header list prefixes are unreliable for some control-word columns, so the participant's List column gives trial_list. The control words sheet re-extracts cells already in ratings_ and is not read; the additional verbs sheet (72 verbs on affective dimensions, 43 raters) is a different instrument under the stimulus floor and is not built. DECOMPORSI appears twice in list 3, so trial_position separates the two ratings. Age, sex and education are participant-level and not carried. Earlier thread #1197 (emailed); from the #1160 list via #2983. See data/sensorimotor_repetto_2022.py.

Description: 140 four-option multiple-choice vocabulary items (Vocabulary Size Test format: a target word in a short carrier sentence, four paraphrase options), administered to the same 275 Chinese university EFL learners, scored 0/1 for correctness. Reference: Yang, C., Yu, X., & Li, H. (2026). Relationship among motivation, vocabulary learning strategies and the breadth of vocabulary knowledge: A structural equation modeling study on second language learning. PLOS One, 20(9).
Notes: The source records the chosen option TEXT, which is nominal. It is scored against an answer key derived from the responses and then verified exactly against the deposit's own "Total Score" column: the derived key reproduces that column for 275/275 respondents, maximum absolute difference 0, across all 140 items. The processing script re-derives and re-asserts that reproduction on every run and refuses to write the table otherwise. "Total Score" itself is dropped as a composite. Item codes v001_see..v140_limpid carry the source's own target word, so they are reversible to the header. Item text in hand but not shipped: the items are the published Vocabulary Size Test (Nation & Beglar, 2007), which has no rights-register row. Description: The 22-item Public Health Clinic Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire (PHC-PSQ) on pharmacy services, answered on a 1-10 satisfaction scale by 400 outpatients at three randomly selected Malaysian public health clinics. Reference: Ahmad, N., Ismail, A., & Gan, Y. N. (2020). Factors associated with patient satisfaction towards pharmacy services among out-patients attending public health clinics: Questionnaire development and its application.
Notes: Complete matrix: 8,800 rows, no missing cells, no fractional values. Item codes are the source's own column names. Three subscales of one instrument administered as one form on one scale, so not split; the multi_scale* warning is the A/B/C domain prefixes. Nested observed ranges (1-10 to 4-10) are category non-use on a 10-point scale, not separate scales. irw-validate's rights_register warning on C1-C3 (Connor-Davidson) is a FALSE POSITIVE: those are the convenience-of-location items, labelled Parking / Public Transport / Home, and the deposit holds no resilience measure. Item text not shipped: variable labels are terse topic keys, not stems, and the 1-10 anchors have no value labels; the wording is in the open-access paper and the instrument is study-authored, so a later pass is cheap and carries no third-party rights question.

Description: The Brazilian Portuguese Positive Oral Health and Well-Being questionnaire (B-POHW), 19 items on a 0-3 agreement scale (0 = Discordo totalmente to 3 = Concordo totalmente), answered by the 209-respondent cross-cultural adaptation sample. Notes: id is the row index: the deposit supplies no identifier column. The file also holds a second administration (RPOHW1-16, RBem_estar1-4) answered by only 54 respondents; it is NOT shipped, for two independent reasons -- 54 is below the N>=100 floor, and the retest has 16 oral-health items against the first application's 15, so the item correspondence is unestablished and a positional match would produce a plausibly wrong wave column. Six *_total columns and six empty section-header columns are dropped. Item text not shipped and the levels differ: variable labels (stems) are absent for all 19 items, value labels (the four Portuguese anchors) are present for all 19 -- option-only, and the stems are one hop away in the published adaptation paper, so shipping the anchors alone is ruled out. B-POHW is an adaptation of a third-party instrument, so the stems need both the original's and the adaptation's terms ruled on.

Notes: id is the row index: the deposit supplies no identifier column. 9,598 rows rather than 9,600 because TWO isolated out-of-range cells were set to missing -- O38 held a single 12 and O56 a single 5 on a 1-4 scale, each one cell out of 160 and every other value in range, which is a data-entry slip rather than a differently-scaled item; nulling them costs 2 observations where dropping the items would cost 320. Description: Agreement with 64 political statements -- 16 per topic across climate change, COVID-19 policy, criminal justice and immigration, 8 true and 8 false in each -- rated on a 7-point scale before and after a research task by 2,858 UK adults in two randomised trials around the 2024 general election. A complete pre/post panel, 365,824 responses. resp is stored AGREE-FIRST: 1 = agree, 7 = disagree, so a lower value means more agreement. treat is the within-subject manipulation (each participant researched two of the four topics); cov_arm is the between-subject randomisation (chatbot vs Google search in study 2, prompted vs default-prompted chatbot in study 3); itemcov_ground_truth marks whether the statement is true.
Reference: Luettgau, L., Kirk, H. R., Hackenburg, K., Bergs, J., Davidson, H., Ogden, H., Siddarth, D., Huang, S., & Summerfield, C. (2026). Conversational AI increases political knowledge as effectively as self-directed internet search. PNAS Nexus, 5(10), pgag305.
